current_behaviour: System Admin mutations (create org unit, set maintenance mode, change role, etc.) produce 'Cannot reach training system' error message even when the error is a server-side validation failure (4xx) or permission error (403). User cannot distinguish network failure from a server error rejecting their change.
expected_behaviour: Error messages must accurately classify the failure: network failure vs server validation vs authentication vs authorisation. A 403 or 422 must say what is wrong, not pretend the server is unreachable.
reproduction: Log in as system_admin. Attempt a System Console mutation that fails (e.g. create a duplicate org unit). Observe generic 'Cannot reach training system' toast or alert.
evidence: Tested by user 2026-08-31. Code inspection: some System Console handlers call e.message directly or use apiErr() on a TypeError path that bypasses the structured {kind:'http'} error. The api() function already throws correctly-structured errors; callers must use apiErr(e) which extracts e.msg.
root_cause: System Console mutation handlers were written before the structured error system was finalised. Some handlers read e.message directly from catch blocks instead of apiErr(e).
dependencies: api() structured error throws; apiErr() helper; System Console error handlers in connected-frontend/index.html
risk: System admins receive misleading errors for routine validation failures. Support burden increases. Admins may retry operations thinking the network is down.
implementation_plan: Audit all System Console error handlers. Replace any direct e.message or e.toString() usage with apiErr(e). Ensure {kind:'http'} errors with a specific message show that message, not a network fallback. See frontend.md: use apiErr(e) for all error display.
test_plan: Test: trigger a 422 validation error from a System Console mutation. Assert error toast shows the validation message not 'Cannot reach training system'. Trigger a real network failure. Assert 'Cannot reach training system' shows.
status: Audit System Console catch blocks for e.message vs apiErr(e). Replace all direct e.message reads with apiErr(e).

current_behaviour: api() already throws structured {kind:'network'|'http'|'auth'|'cancelled'|'invalid_response'} objects. apiErr(e) extracts e.msg from any of these. However some catch blocks (especially in System Console and older sections) use e.message directly or construct error strings without calling apiErr(). This causes network-error text to appear when the real failure is a server-side 4xx with a specific message.
expected_behaviour: All error display must call apiErr(e). No catch block must read e.message directly for user display. Network failures must say 'Cannot reach training system'. 4xx errors must show the specific message the backend provided.
reproduction: Reproduce P0-SYSADMIN-01: trigger a 422/403 from a System Console action. Observe the error message shown. It should show the specific error, not 'Cannot reach training system'.
evidence: Code inspection: multiple System Console handlers use e.message (e.g. line 6653: msg.textContent='Error: '+(apiErr(e)) — this is CORRECT; but others may not be). Comprehensive audit required.
root_cause: Inconsistent error handling patterns in older sections of connected-frontend. apiErr() was added later and not backfilled everywhere.
dependencies: None
risk: Misleading errors across many surfaces. Users misdiagnose failures.
implementation_plan: Audit all catch blocks in connected-frontend/index.html. Replace any direct e.message, e.toString(), or String(e) usage with apiErr(e) for user-visible error display. Add error classification layer (see addendum Section AJ) if needed.
test_plan: Test: trigger 400/403/422/500/network-failure. Assert each shows correct category of error message.
status: Audit all catch blocks. Replace e.message with apiErr(e) for display. Add classification if needed.
